Try this

Tap + → Fill-up. Type 3575 into Total, tap Litres, type 2610 — €/L computes itself. Tap the odometer, type 91880, then Save.
Then try the honest paths: type an odometer lower than the last reading · turn Full tank off · save with no odometer at all · start typing and hit Discard.
Watch the interval, not just the fill. The saved economy counts 43,60 L, not your 26,10 — the 24 July fill in the feed recorded litres with no odometer, so the fold rule puts them in this interval. The moment says so.

What this prototype is testing

Speed. Two numbers and a reading is the whole interaction — no scrolling, no dropdowns, no confirmation step. If it does not feel like seconds, the design is wrong.

The computed third. Whether watching €/L fill itself reads as helpful or as the app editing your input. It is labelled computed and stays inkSoft to say "not yours".

The one spring. Whether the saved moment feels like the record landing or like praise. It is the only spring in the app; everything else is a 150 ms fade.

Honest by construction

A reading below 91.240 km names the conflicting record and offers to open it — the build's current message does neither. Save stays disabled while it conflicts.

Save with no odometer and the moment says Not measured — no odometer on this fill, and where the litres went. Turn Full tank off and it says the same for a partial. Neither is styled as an error, and the record still saves.

The missed-fill switch appears only when it can be true, and states its cost the moment it is on.

Two things deliberately not simulated

The station and date chips are inert — they open fitted pickers, which sheet 03 already specifies and which would add a layer without testing anything new here. And the keypad is Koi's own, not the iOS numeric pad: the sheet owns its full height, so the pad is drawn rather than summoned.
